skill.name: zoom-out
skill.description: Guide an agent to explain unfamiliar code from a higher level, including relevant modules, callers, and domain vocabulary.
skill.summary: Ask an agent for a higher-level map of unfamiliar code.
skill.author: mattpocock

security_audit.summary: Static analysis found no suspicious patterns in the single prompt-only SKILL.md file. I found no semantic prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or code execution behavior. No remediation is required.

content.user_title: Map Code Context With Zoom Out
content.value_statement: Unfamiliar code is hard to change when modules, callers, and domain terms are unclear. This skill prompts Claude, Codex, or Claude Code to explain the broader map before implementation.
actual_capabilities: Prompts the assistant to explain unfamiliar code at a higher abstraction level.
Requests a map of relevant modules and callers in the project.
Asks for project domain glossary vocabulary when describing code.
Supports codebase onboarding before detailed implementation work.
Works as a prompt-only skill for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
limitations: Does not inspect code by itself; the connected AI tool must read the project files.
Does not generate diagrams unless the user asks for a diagram format.
Does not replace detailed debugging, testing, or security review.
Best results require access to the relevant repository context.

use_cases.title: Onboard To Legacy Code
use_cases.description: Understand the main modules, callers, and domain terms before changing an unfamiliar area.

use_cases.title: Review Cross-Module Impact
use_cases.description: See how a feature path fits into surrounding architecture before planning work.

use_cases.title: Prepare Context For Pairing
use_cases.description: Ask Claude, Codex, or Claude Code for a higher-level map before requesting edits.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Code Map
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the zoom-out skill on the current file. Explain what this area does, which modules call it, and the key domain terms.

prompt_templates.title: Trace Feature Context
prompt_templates.prompt: Zoom out from this feature. Map the relevant modules, callers, data flow, and ownership boundaries before suggesting any changes.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Architectural Options
prompt_templates.prompt: Zoom out across this subsystem. Identify adjacent modules, tradeoffs, and risks that affect a refactor plan.

prompt_templates.title: Build A Change Brief
prompt_templates.prompt: Use zoom-out context for this complex change. Produce a concise architecture brief with callers, dependencies, glossary terms, and open questions.

output_examples.input: I am in an unfamiliar payment workflow. Zoom out before I edit it.
output: A module map naming checkout, invoices, payment providers, and account ledger boundaries.
A caller summary showing which flows reach the payment workflow.
A glossary of project-specific terms used by the payment code.

output_examples.input: Before refactoring this service, explain how it fits into the application.
output: A higher-level explanation of the service responsibility and neighboring modules.
A list of likely downstream effects to check before changing behavior.
Open questions for missing ownership, data flow, or integration details.

best_practices: Use it before editing files in an unfamiliar area.
Share the specific file, feature, or workflow that needs broader context.
Ask for callers, module boundaries, and glossary terms in the same response.
anti_patterns: Do not use it as a substitute for reading critical code paths.
Do not ask for broad context without naming the area of code.
Do not rely on it for security conclusions without a separate audit.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It asks the assistant to explain unfamiliar code from a higher-level project perspective.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it run code or commands?
faq.answer: No. The skill is prompt-only and contains no executable code.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it before changing a code area that has unclear modules, callers, or domain terms.

faq.question: Can it find every caller automatically?
faq.answer: It depends on the connected AI tool and its access to the repository.

faq.question: Does it replace code review?
faq.answer: No. It provides orientation, but detailed review and testing remain necessary.
